To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of time delays (deterministic, or random) can significantly degrade the performance of a dynamic load-balancing policy and that the performance degradation can be reduced by down-scaling the load transfer.

(i) the performance of load-balancers in a cluster of nodes is significantly altered by the presence of communication delays; (ii) the effect of such delays can be predicted by means of the stochastic model developed herein; and (iii) the effect of the delays can be minimized by weakening the load-balancing policy.

(i) the presence of delay, either deterministic or random, can lead to a severe deterioration in the performance of the load-balancing policy, and (ii) one way to remedy such an adverse effect is to weaken the policy's load-transfer mechanism so that the loads are transferred less aggressively (or discouraged) as the delay increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a load-balanced system in which the communication delays are large and fluctuate randomly.
the development of a methodology for the analysis and prediction of the performance of load-balanced systems in which there are time delays between the nodes.
the analysis and design of distributed systems that are robust to the presence of time delays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the performance of a dynamic load-balancing algorithm is highly sensitive to the presence and magnitude of delays in the system, and that the uncertainty associated with the delays can be even more detrimental to the algorithm's performance.
the presence of delays, deterministic or stochastic, is detrimental to load balancing, and the magnitude of the degradation is proportional to the magnitude of the delays.
the performance of load-balancers can be significantly degraded by the presence of delays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effect of time delays on load balancing can be mitigated by weakening the load-balancing policy in the presence of time delays.

the performance of load-balanced systems is significantly degraded by time delays, and that a simple remedy to this problem is to down-scale the load-balancing policy so as to reduce the amount of load transfer between nodes.
the performance of the load balancing is significantly affected by the presence of time delays and that this effect can be modeled by a stochastic dynamical-equations approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in a system with random delays, a load-balancing mechanism should not be overly aggressive.
the presence of random delay in a load-balancing system can significantly affect the performance of the system.
, for load-balancing policies, the effect of delay is not a negligible factor that can be ignored, but is a significant one that must be taken into account.
